_comment: Fictional observation corpus for the demo tenant. Written by hand so that
the finds in history.json are genuinely discoverable by semantic search
Clusters are deliberate: tiramisu praise supports the dessert repricing
find, Saturday wait complaints support the waitlist find, and lunch
inquiries support the lunch find. Parking complaints are intentional noise —
a real signal the Analyst should recognise as low-value because the owner
cannot fix a public parking supply.
days_ago is relative to the seed run, so the corpus is always 'the last
eight weeks' whenever it is loaded, and history.json stays aligned with it.
Source names are generic: we do not scrape real platforms.

observations.content: The tiramisu here is genuinely the best I have had in this city, and I have tried a lot of them. Light, not soggy, actual espresso flavor.
Came for the pasta, stayed for the tiramisu. My wife said it was better than what she had in Rome, which is a sentence I did not expect to hear.
Solid neighborhood Italian. The dessert is the standout — that tiramisu is worth the trip on its own.
Still thinking about the tiramisu from last night. Criminally underpriced for what it is.
We order two tiramisus every single time, one to eat there and one to take home. It is the reason we keep coming back.
Best dessert on the street by a mile. I would pay double for that tiramisu, honestly.
If anyone is looking for dessert downtown, Rosa's tiramisu is the answer. Not close.
Food was good, service a little slow, but that tiramisu made up for everything.
Homemade tiramisu that actually tastes homemade. You can tell it is not coming out of a freezer box.
Took my parents to Rosa's. Dad does not like desserts. Dad ate an entire tiramisu.
The tiramisu is the single best thing on the menu and it is somehow the cheapest dessert they offer.
Everything was lovely but the tiramisu is on another level. Get two.
Weekly tiramisu ranking thread: Rosa's still number one, still seven dollars, still confusing.
I have started bringing out of town guests here specifically so they can try the tiramisu. Never misses.
Waited fifty minutes on a Saturday with no way to know how long it would actually be. Food was good but we nearly left twice.
Showed up at 7 on a Saturday, told it would be twenty minutes, left after forty five. No list, no updates, just standing by the door.
Great food, terrible wait management. You stand in a doorway blocking servers because there is nowhere to put people.
Saturday night is a scrum. If they took a phone number and texted you when a table opened this would be a five star review.
Second Saturday in a row we could not get a table and could not get a straight answer on the wait. Going elsewhere.
Rosa's on a Saturday: incredible food, an hour of your life standing up. Go on a Tuesday.
No reservations and no waitlist is a strange choice for a place this popular on weekends.
Weeknight visit was perfect, quick and calm. Weekend visit was chaos. Same kitchen, completely different experience.
Waited forty minutes past the quoted time on a Saturday. Nobody checked on us once while we stood there.
The wait on weekends is the only thing keeping this from being my favorite restaurant in the neighborhood.
Anyone know if Rosa's takes reservations yet? Gave up on a Saturday last month after a long wait.
Turned away on Saturday at 8pm. They said an hour and a half. We ate at Lucca's instead, which was fine but not as good.
Where is everyone eating lunch near the courthouse? Options seem thin and I am tired of the sandwich place.
Downtown lunch thread: anything decent and sit-down within walking distance of the county building?
Wish they were open for lunch. I work two blocks away and would be here twice a week.
Nine of us tried to find somewhere to sit down for lunch downtown today and ended up eating at desks again.
Only complaint: dinner only. A lunch pasta special would clean up with the office crowd around here.
Is Rosa's Trattoria open midday? Their website says dinner but I have seen the lights on.
New office tower on the block means about four hundred more people needing lunch. Somebody should open earlier.
Came for an early dinner because they do not do lunch. Would absolutely come at noon if they did.
Lunch options near the courthouse are genuinely bad. The Italian place is dinner only which is a shame.
Anyone else notice how many people are wandering around at noon looking for somewhere to sit down and eat?
Called four times to ask about a large party and nobody picked up. Ended up booking somewhere else.
Phone rings and rings during dinner service. Understandable but frustrating when you just want to ask one question.
No answer on the phone, no online anything. If you want to know something you have to walk over.
Tried to check if the patio was open before driving over. No answer. Drove over. Patio was closed.
Wanted to order a whole tiramisu for a birthday. Could not reach anyone to ask. Gave up.
Lovely place but essentially unreachable by phone after 5pm.
Parking around here is impossible after six. Circled for fifteen minutes.
Food excellent, parking a nightmare. Not really their fault but be warned.
Had to park four blocks away and walk in the rain. The garage nearby was full.
Great meal. Terrible street parking situation in this whole district though.
Would come more often if parking were easier. Not much they can do about it I suppose.
Take the bus if you can. Parking is the worst part of the evening and the food is the best.
Second time we have circled for a spot. Consider a validated garage deal?
Parking is rough but the meal is worth it. Bring quarters for the meters.
Eight years of coming here and it has never once been a bad meal. The cacio e pepe is perfect.
Family run, feels like it. Rosa came out and talked to our table for ten minutes about the sauce.
The lasagna is the real deal. Layers you can count. Portion big enough for two.
Reliable, warm, unpretentious. Exactly what a neighborhood Italian should be.
Homemade pasta you can taste the difference in. The bolognese has clearly been going all day.
Took a first date here and it went well entirely because of the atmosphere. Candles, small room, no TV.
Bread comes warm and they refill it without asking. Small thing, matters a lot.
Our anniversary spot for six years running. Never a reason to try anywhere else.
The gnocchi were light as air. I have no idea how they do that at this price point.
Good wine list for a small place. The house red is a steal.
Brought a group of eight and they handled it gracefully on a weeknight. Kitchen kept up.
Best meal I have had in Columbus this year and it is a room with fourteen tables.
Consistent. Been coming a year, never a miss. That is harder than people think.
Everything about this place feels like someone's actual grandmother is in the back. Because she basically is.
Walked in on a Wednesday with no wait and had one of the best plates of pasta of my life.
Server was clearly covering the whole room alone. Did great, but should not have had to.
Slow between courses on a busy night, but everyone was kind about it.
Our server knew the menu cold and steered us away from something we would not have liked. Rare.
Took twenty minutes to get the check at the end. Front of house is stretched thin on weekends.
They remembered us from a visit two months ago. That is not something you can fake.
One server for the whole floor on a Thursday. She was excellent but visibly underwater.
Genuinely warm service. They treat regulars and first timers the same, which I notice.
Service is friendly but understaffed at peak. Worth the patience.
Prices are more than fair for the quality. Cheaper than the place down the street for better food.
Honestly underpriced. I keep expecting the bill to be higher than it is.
Great value. Two mains, a bottle, and dessert came in under ninety.
Rosa's is somehow still the cheapest good Italian downtown. Not sure how that math works for them.
The dessert prices in particular feel like they have not been updated in years.
Fair prices, generous portions. We took half of it home.
You could charge more for this and I would still come. Please do not, but you could.
Sat on the patio on a warm evening and it was perfect. Wish they used it more.
The patio was closed on a beautiful seventy degree night, which seemed like a waste.
Patio season and half the good spots downtown still have their outdoor seating stacked up.
Outdoor tables are the best seats in the house. String lights, quiet street.
Asked for the patio and they said it was not set up that night. Would have made the evening.
Best patios downtown thread — Rosa's would be top three if they ever actually opened theirs.
